route: depth CNN (64-D latent) + 324-D proprio history -> MLP (no fine scan)

environment.eval: pixi -e eval: torch 2.14.1+cpu (PyPI CPU wheel), MuJoCo 3.11, numpy
environment.deploy: pixi -e demo: torch 2.14.1+cpu (same PyPI CPU wheel), MuJoCo 3.11, ROS 2 Humble
environment.train: pixi -e train: torch 2.14.1+cu130 (all three envs on the same torch line)

official_level_run.command: pixi run -e eval robocon-eval run --robot blackW --part 2 --level plum_1 --policy plum_depth_final_v1 --profile official --out artifacts/part2_evals/torch214/plum_1.jsonl --result artifacts/part2_evals/torch214/plum_1.json
official_level_run.note: official spawn (dy=0, yaw=0); this is the scored-attempt configuration

spawn_offset_grid.note: dy/dyaw applied after settle, before the policy starts; 20 s runs, same official profile; the policy is deterministic, so the grid measures fragility, not seed noise

deployment_composed.note: real sim_node+rl_sim route trace (full-field frame, composed attempt): the depth policy crosses entry platform + pile field; on the exit platform (field x=6.80) the route switches to vt_band_v1 via /policy_switch, brakes 0.6 s with reverse velocity, stands 2 s, then walks the 0.2 m exit step at 0.45 m/s. The depth actor's own exit descent is knife-edge in the deployment stack, hence the split. Handing over on the pile field is invalid (the wheeled expert drops a wheel between piles), and switching without braking carries the 2 m/s momentum off the platform; both were measured. Repeats: plum_comp_v5r1/r2 both route-PASS and judge-success.

cxx_inference_parity.note: rl_sim RL_DEPTH_DEBUG=1 dumps policy input (obs history + raw metric depth) and raw action; Python policy() on the same input returns the same action bit-for-bit (6 consecutive inference frames)

renderer_parity.tool: sim_node --depth-self-test <scene.xml> vs mujoco.Renderer in eval env

metrics.end_pose_note: success latched ~2.4 m past the exit at ~41 deg tilt; legal under the 75 deg fall rule
limitations: The actor's own exit-platform descent is knife-edge: it passes the official single-level run at the exact spawn, but the spawn grid above is 2/15 and the deployment stack tips off the exit edge; the demo route therefore composes the descent with a wheeled expert.
Robustness retraining (wider spawn/velocity randomization, exit-descent reward) is the recommended next step; the single-level evidence here is the scored configuration, not a robustness claim.
